findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup allows bypassing blocked emails
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the input's case, and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving or enforce case-insensitive uniqueness. Because `User` does not downcase `email` prior to validation and PostgreSQL `=` comparisons on string columns are case-sensitive, a user can bypass a blocked email entry simply by capitalizing any character in the address (e.g., `Bad@spammers.org` vs. `bad@spammers.org`).

findings.title: Side-effecting validation increments `match_count` twice per signup attempt
findings.body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record during model validation. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is evaluated first and then `user.save` is called unconditionally, running validations a second time. As a result, a single signup attempt with a blocked or tracked email executes `BlockedEmail.should_block?` twice and increments `match_count` by 2 instead of 1.
